Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners are the owner of the land bearing survey Nos.147, 148/1, 148/2 ad-measuring area of 0.051 and 0.064 hectares respectively situated from Village-Kakni to Navadiha, Tehsil-Ludra, Disrict Surguja (C.G.).

He would further submit that out of the total area, the area admeasuring one acre was Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17368 acquired by the authority for construction of the road under the Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojna Scheme (for short' the PMGSY Scheme') without making payment of compensation.

sentences.text: He would further submit that the claim of the petitioners have not been considered on the ground that there is no provision under the PMGSY Scheme to make payment of compensation.

He would also submit that the issue is no more res integra and the Hon'ble Division Bench in the matter of State of Chhattsigarh and others Vs. Hari Singh Chandra and others passed in Writ Appeal No.351 of 2019, dated 20.10.2021

sentences.text: 2) On the other hand, Mr. Diwan, learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the Union of India would submit that there is no scheme to make payment of compensation under the PMGSY Scheme.
He would further submit that the land was provided by the State Government to the Central Government for construction of the road under that Scheme.

He would further contend that as the land was provided by the State, therefore, if the petitioners are entitled for any compensation,
the same would be paid by the State Government.

3) Mr. Samant, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State would submit that there was already a kachha road on the land of the petitioners and the respondents upgraded the said road and the road has already been constructed.
It is also submitted that the land of the petitioners was never Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17368 acquired or used for construction of any road.
It is further submitted that a resolution was passed by the Gram Sabha on 09.04.2022.

It is also argued that the petitioners ought to have moved an application before the Collector within a period of one year from the date of construction of the road whereas the petitioners have filed this petition after 14 years and therefore,
the present petition deserves to be dismissed.
4) I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the documents on record.
5) Admittedly, the petitioners are the owner of Survey No.148/1,148/2 and 147 admeasuring 0.051 and 0.064 hectares respectively.
Survey No.147 admeasuring 0.064 hectare was utilized in construction of road under the PMGSY Scheme in the year 2010.
It is also pleaded that without taking any consent of the petitioners, the road was constructed and no compensation has been paid till date to the petitioners.

6) The Hon'ble Division Bench in the matter of Hari Singh Chandra (supra), while dealing with the issue in paras 10,11 and 12 held as under :
"10.
That the land of the petitioner was utilized for construction of the road in question, is an admitted position.

Though contention is advanced by the learned State counsel that land was obtained for the purpose of road construction after obtaining due consent, no materials have been placed before the Court to demonstrate the factum of obtaining consent from the petitioner.
The document at Annexure R/2, on which reliance was placed by the learned State counsel, is dated 18.04.2018.
It is not understood under what circumstances such Panchanama had to be obtained from some of the villagers in the year 2018 when the land was utilized in the year 2005.

That apart, it is rightly submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.1/petitioner that even this document does not reflect the name or Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17368 signature of the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
From the discussions above, it is evident that the land of the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of road construction without following due process of law,
resulting in violation of Article 300- A of the Constitution of India.

Taking note of above, the learned Single Judge had directed demarcation of the land of the petitioner which was utilized for the purpose of road construction and thereafter, to grant compensation in accordance with the Act of 2013.

12. Resultantly, while upholding the order of learned Single Judge to the extent of demarcation of the land, in view of submission of Mr. Rakesh Pandey, we modify the direction of grant of compensation in the light of the provisions of the Act of 2013 to the effect that compensation shall be paid under the provisions of the Act of 1894."
7) Taking into consideration the fact that the land of the petitioners was utilized for construction of road, no compensation was paid, therefore, the present petition at this juncture is disposed of with the direction to the authorities to grant compensation in the light of the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
